questions.question: ______in a particular direction is velocity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__Explanation:-__

__
 
• The speed of a moving particle measures how fast it is moving.
 
• It does not tell about the direction of motion while in the case of velocity speed it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• So, the velocity of a moving particle measures the rate of change in position during its entire motion. i.e speed of a particle in a given direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acceleration

 
 
• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• Acceleration is a vector quantity as it has both magnitude and direction. It also the second derivative of position with respect to time or it is the first derivative of velocity with respect to time.
 
• Instantaneous acceleration is defined as the ratio of change in velocity during a given time interval such that the time interval goes to zero.
 
 
 
• **Displacement**
 
 
• It is the shortest distance covered by a body in a definite direction.
 
• It is a vector quantity.
 
• It can be positive, Negative, or Zero.
 
• The unit of displacement is a meter(m).
 
 

 
• Distance

 
 
• The length of the actual path covered by a moving object in a given time.
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
• It is always positive.
 
• The unit of distance is a meter (m).

questions.question: Which road plan in India was the first attempt for the Road Development Programme between 1943-1963?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagpur Road Plan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first 20-year road development plan** is also known as the **"Nagpur Road Plan" **in popular culture.
 
• In **1943**, the government convened a **conference of chief engineers at Nagpur** to discuss road development and construction.
 
• The conference is popularly known as the **Nagpur road plan.**
 
• The Nagpur road plan sets a target** road length of 16 km per 100 square kilometers **of the nation.
 
• Although the Nagpur Road Development Plan was intended to be completed between 1943 and 1963, it was actually **completed two years earlier.**
 
• The Nagpur road plan has a **5,32,700 km goal road length.**
 
• **Star and grid are the patterns** that are applied to the roadways in the Nagpur road plan.
 
• For the Nagpur road plan, the** development allowance is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bombay Road Plan:**

 
 
• The Indian road system was intended to be significantly expanded as part of the** Twenty-Year Plan (Bombay Plan) (1961–1981),** particularly the **National and State Highways.**
 
 
 
• **Lucknow Road Plan:**
 
 
• **​​**The **third 20-year road plan** was this one (1981-2001).

questions.question: In August 2022, the "SMILE-75 Initiative" was launched by Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. What is the objective of this scheme?

options.text: To provide education and training to the weaker sections of the society
To improve immunisation coverage for children and pregnant women in India
To accelerate the development of biopharmaceuticals
To make our cities/town and municipal areas begging-free.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To make our cities/town and municipal areas begging-free.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

 
• Under the “SMILE-75” Initiative, 75 Municipal Corporations will undertake comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of begging in the spirit of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav.
 
• Municipal Corporations, in collaboration with NGOs and other stakeholders, will cover several comprehensive welfare measures for persons who are engaged in the act of begging, with a focus extensively on rehabilitation, provision of medical facilities, counselling, awareness, education, skill development, economic linkages and convergence with other Government welfare programmes etc.
 
• The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment has also allocated a total budget of Rs.100 crore for the SMILE project for the coming years till** 2025-26.**
 
• It seeks to develop a support mechanism for the holistic rehabilitation of those engaged in the act of begging.
 
• Implementing Ministry: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
• It includes the sub-scheme of Comprehensive Rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of Begging.
 
• Objectives:
 
 
• To make cities/towns and municipal areas begging-free.
 
• To make a strategy for comprehensive rehabilitation of the persons engaged in the act of begging through the coordinated action of various stakeholders.

questions.question: In which year were the 73rd and 74th amendments passed by the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments were passed by Parliament in December 1992.
 
• **73rd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 has added a new part IX consisting of 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• The 73rd Amendment envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures. 
 
• The Constitution was amended by the 73rd *Amendment **to make the three-tier of democracy* more powerful and effective.
 
• It empowered local governments rural, as constitutional entities and initiated a new chapter in the process of democratic decentralization in India. 
 
• The provisions of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, To hold regular elections under the local government bodies have been made compulsory. 
 
 
 
• 74th Amendment Act:
 
 
• Part IXA in the Constitution, which deals with Municipalities in an article **243 P to 243 ZG,** has been introduced under the 74th Amendment Act.
 
• The act provides for a five-year term of office for every municipality from the date of its first meeting.
 
• The elections to constitute a municipality shall be completed before the expiry of its duration of five years. 
 
• However, it can be dissolved before the completion of its term.
 
• If the municipality is dissolved before the expiry of its term, the elections for constituting a new municipality must be **completed within 6 months from the date of its dissolution.**
 
• A municipality constituted after its premature dissolution shall continue only for the remainder of the term.
 
• If the remainder of the period is less than 6 months it is not necessary to hold elections for the remaining period but a fresh election for the entire term is mandated.
 
• Persons who have attained the age of 21 years are eligible to contest the municipal elections i.e no person shall be disqualified if he is less than 25 years of age and has attained 21 years of age to contest in municipal elections.

questions.question: Vetti tax that is mentioned in the inscriptions of the Chola dynasty was taken in _________ form.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forced labour.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vetti tax **is the most frequently mentioned tax in the inscription of** Cholas who ruled in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Vetti was a form of **forced labour tax.**
 
• It was levied from common people.
 
• Common people were forced to work for the king or their village landlords without any wages.
 
• **The Chola dynasty **is considered one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the world's history.
 
• Land revenue and trade tax were the main sources of income during the **Chola period.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Chola Empire of the South emerged in the ​9th century AD (850-1279 AD).
 
 
• The founder of the Chola Dynasty - **Vijayalaya**
 
• Vijayalaya captured Tanjore in 850 AD.
 
• The greatest Chola ruler was **Rajaraja** (985-1014 AD) and Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD).
 
• Rajaraja built the Brihadeshwara temple/Rajarajeshwara temple (attributed to Shiva) at Tanjore.
 
• **Rajendra I** conquered Orissa, Bengal, Burma, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The Chola dynasty was at its zenith during his reign.
 
• Rajendra I defeated the Pala king Mahipala and took the title of Gangaikondachola and built a city called Gangaikondacholapuram.
 
• King Rajasimha built the **Kailashnath temple** at Kancheepuram.
 
• Parantak I built the Koranganatha temple at Srini wasanllur.
 
• Rajaraja II built the Airawteshwar temple at Darasuram.
 
• Kullotung III built the Kampahreshwar temple at Tribhuvan.
 
• The last ruler of the Chola dynasty was Rajendra III.
 
• Land revenue and trade tax were the main sources of income.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Water is a cyclic resource.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water is a cyclic resource, as it is present in different states and abundant supplies around the globe.
 
• **A cyclic resource** is what can be **formed, again and again, Similarly water is a cyclic resource.**
 
• **The water** from the sea, river, ocean, etc. evaporates and condenses to form clouds.
 
• When the rain occurs water from these clouds comes onto earth and flows down into water resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The hydrological cycle is also known as the **water cycle;** it is the normal water recycling system on Earth. 
 
• It is the total of all processes in which water moves from the land and ocean surface to the atmosphere and back in form of precipitation.
 
• Though water is an** abiotic component of the environment**, it is not described as one since water carries many biotic components in it which are often crucial for the sustenance of life on earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water is, indeed a** renewable resource.**
 
• Water has** three states.**
 
• Water or Fresh Water is a renewable Natural Resource.
 
• However, it should be noted that freshwater is a non-renewable energy resource.
 
• Water is used as a power generation tool by using turbines and steam boilers.
 
• Water also acts as one of the five elements which enable humans to live on this planet.
 
• Water is a **cyclic resource as it is used and reused.**
 
• **About 71% **of the planetary water is found in the oceans.
 
• The remaining is held as freshwater in glaciers and ice caps, groundwater sources, lakes, soil moisture, atmosphere, streams, and within life.
 
• **About 59% **of the water on the land surface evaporates and returns to the atmosphere.
 
• The remaining run-off on the surface penetrates the ground or a part of it becomes glaciers.

questions.question: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim, Xuan Zang, came to the Indian subcontinent about __ __ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1400**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim, Xuan Zang, came to the Indian subcontinent about** 1400 years ago.**

 
• A Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller, and translator who travelled to India in the seventh century.
 
• He described the interaction between Chinese Buddhism and Indian Buddhism during the early Tang dynasty.
 
• The primary aim of the visit of Hiuen Tsang to India was to gain knowledge of Buddhism and collect its religious texts.
 
• As he did not get the permission of the Chinese emperor to visit India, he slipped away from there in 629 A.D.
 
• He remained at the University of Nalanda for about five years.
 
• He also participated in one of the religious assemblies called by Harsha at Prayag.
 
• He became famous for his seventeen-year overland journey to India.
 
• He visited India during the reign of Harshavardhan who came to admire him for his deep devotion to Buddhism.

questions.question: Identify an example of decomposers that are found in the bottom of a pond.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flagellates.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flagellates are found in the bottom of a pond.**

 
 
• They are an example of Protozoa.
 
• Protozoa are found in **soil, freshwater, and seawater.**
 
• Some are found in the body of other organisms and are pathogenic. These are unicellular organisms with eukaryotic cells.
 
• There is great variation in cell structure, organs of locomotion and modes of nutrition among protozoa.
 
• These organisms reproduce by **simple cell division.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Zooplankton **is present on the second trophic level in a food chain in the aquatic ecosystem.
 
• They are primary consumers as they eat **phytoplankton **(producers) and are themselves in turn eaten by small fishes (secondary consumers).
 
• **Jellyfish **and sea jellies are the informal common names given to the medusa-phase of certain gelatinous members of the subphylum Medusozoa, a major part of the phylum Cnidaria.

questions.question: The __ __ is a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution** is a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
 
• The Indian Constitution is the **longest in the world.**
 
• It has been written in **145,000 words.**
 
• It was composed between the years 1947 and 1950.
 
• Originally, it** had 395 articles, 8 schedules, and 22 parts and came into effect on 26 January 1950.**
 
• The articles have now been increased to** 448 after many amendments.**
 
• It is 30 times longer than the American Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of E-Commerce?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Late response to customer needs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A late response to customer needs is **NOT** an **advantage of E-Commerce**.
 
• **Electronic commerce** is known as e-commerce.
 
• The purchasing and selling of goods and services, or the sending of money or data, over an electronic network, typically the internet, is referred to as an e-commerce business.
 
• E-commerce also refers to any type of business transaction in which the parties communicate with one another virtually rather than in person.
 
• **Advantages of E-Commerce:**
 
 
• Faster buying/selling procedure
 
• Buying/Selling 24/7
 
• Low operational costs with better quality services
 
• Easy to start and manage a business
 
• Cost-Effective including higher Margin
 
• Better Productivity
 
• Allows for product and Price Comparison
 
• No standing in Queues or being placed on hold forever
 
• Ease of communication and superior customization
 
• Enhance convenience
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of E-Commerce:**

 
 
• Industry Online Ticketing
 
• Internet Banking
 
• Electronic auction
 
• Online selling (Buying and Selling of goods)
 
• Online selling (Buying and Selling of services)
 
• Transmitting funds or data

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Director General, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) in September 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Lal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharat Lal** has been appointed as** the Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) in September 2022.**
 
• Bharat Lal, a retired officer from the Gujarat cadre, has been appointed director general of the **National Center for Good Governance (NCGG)**.
 
• He was an Indian Forest Officer from the Gujarat cadre who graduated in 1988, served as the state of Gujarat's resident commissioner in Delhi, and was rumored to be friendly with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who was the state's chief minister at the time.
 
• Lal had previously been chosen to serve as Lokpal's Secretary in December 2021.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances**, Government of India, oversees the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), an independent organization.
 
• It has a branch office in Mussoorie and a head office in New Delhi.
 
• The NCGG was established to support the implementation of governance reforms through research, education, knowledge exchange, and the promotion of sound concepts.
 
• It aims to conduct case studies and policy-relevant research, organize training programs for government employees from India and other developing nations, offer a forum for the exchange of knowledge already in existence, and actively seek out and develop ideas for their implementation in the government, both at the national and international levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As secretary for the Union Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas,** Tarun Kapoor** retired as an IAS officer from the Himachal Pradesh cadre, class of 1987.
 
• The World Health Organization currently employs **Dr. Rajiv Bahl**, who was appointed for a three-year term as Secretary of the Department of Health Research and Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
 
• At Axis Bank, **Pralay Mondal** served as Executive Director and Head of Retail Banking.

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was a contemporary of which Chola king?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni **was a contemporary of **Chola king Rajendra I**.
 
• He also raided the temples of overthrown rulers in the subcontinent throughout his conquests, taking their valuables and idols with him.
 
• At the time, Sultan Mahmud was not a very significant sultan.
 
• However, he attempted to establish himself as a great figure of Islam by destroying temples, particularly the one at Somnath.
 
• The majority of kings in Middle Ages political culture demonstrated their power and military might by assaulting and pillaging the temples of defeated rulers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ghaznavid Empire **was established by **Mahmud of Ghazni,** the first sultan in recorded history. His title indicated that the Caliph of Islam, who oversaw much of what is now Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northern India, continued to be the political and religious head of the empire.
 
• **Rajendra Chola I,** also known as Gangaikonda Chola, Kadaram Kondan, and Rajendra the Great, was a Chola Emperor who ruled from 1014 until 1044 CE.
 
• **Rajendra Chola II, **also known as Rajendradeva Chola, was a Chola emperor who ruled from 1052 to 1064 CE. He was born in 997 CE. After his brother Rajadhiraja I was killed at the Battle of Koppam, he was named Rajendra to succeed him.
 
• **Rajaraja Chola II **was succeeded as ruler of the Cholas by Rajadhiraja Chola II (1166-1178 CE). Rajadhiraja II, a Vikrama Chola maternal grandson, was chosen by Rajaraja Chola II. as he was a sonless man.

questions.question: In April 2022, which scheme was selected for PM's Award for Excellence in Public Administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UDAN**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2022**, the **UDAN scheme** was selected for **PM's Award for Excellence in Public Administration**. 
 
• **The Ministry of Civil Aviation's (MoCA) **main program, the Regional Connectivity Scheme **UDAN (UdeDeshkaAamNagrik)**, has been chosen for the 2020 Prime Minister's Award for Excellence in Public Administration in the category **"Innovation (General) - Central."**
 
• The UDAN system places more emphasis on good governance, qualitative accomplishments, and last mile connection than it does on merely hitting quantitative benchmarks.
 
• Over 92 lakh people have benefited from the 415 UDAN routes that have connected 66 underserved and unserved airports, including heliports, in a short period of five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **"SMILE"** Central Sector programme has been introduced by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment. Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise is referred to as SMILE.
 
• **The Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) programme **was launched by the Indian government in 2015 to address issues with gender inequality and women's empowerment in the nation.
 
• **The "Make in India"** project is built upon four pillars that have been identified as having the potential to stimulate entrepreneurship in India across a variety of industries, not only the manufacturing one.

questions.question: The Sunderban delta is the home of which of the following animal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Royal Bengal Tiger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The largest tiger in the world, **the Royal Bengal Tiger**, lives in the **Sunderbans**, a delta created by the **Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.**
 
• The Sunderbans' marshy delta is home to more than three-fourths of eastern India's Royal Bengal Tigers.
 
• The beautiful and fierce Royal Bengal tigers live in these lush evergreen delta forests.
 
• At the Bay of Bengal, the confluence of the Ganga, Hooghly, and Brahmaputra rivers creates the Sundarban Delta. It is a mangrove wetland with freshwater. India makes up **40% of the marshy delta's **overall area.
 
• The remainder belongs to Bangladesh. These marshes shield the local population from storms and floods that originate in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• There is an abundance of vegetation and fauna in the Sundarban Delta. Mangrove forests of a tree called "Sundari" dominate the area. The name Sundarban comes from this distinctive tree.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Asiatic cheetah** previously ranged from the Arabian Peninsula and the Near East to the Transcaucasus, Kyzylkum Desert, and northern South Asia. However, throughout the 20th century, it became extinct in these areas.
 
• **The Asiatic lion** often referred to as the Indian lion and the Persian lion is a subspecies of Panthera leo that is currently the only one to still exist in the wild outside of India.
 
• The melanistic color variation of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar is known as a **black panther** (Panthera onca). Both species of black panthers have an abundance of their dark pigments, but they also have their characteristic rosettes.
